steps: 1. Identify the conversion ratio connecting systems (e.g. 1 in = 2.54 cm, 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lbs)
2. Set up a ratio table or proportion aligning customary and metric units
3. Multiply or divide by the conversion factor to compute the equivalent measurement

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Bridge Engineering
revealWordProblem.text: The Golden Gate Bridge can hold about 35,924,000 pounds across its full length. An average midsize car has a mass of about 1,524 kilograms. Using 1 kilogram ≈ 2.2 pounds, about how many midsize cars could travel across the bridge at one time? Explain why your answer is an estimate.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A photograph of the Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Convert one car's mass into pounds so both amounts share a unit: 1,524 × 2.2 ≈ 3,353 pounds per car. Then divide the bridge's capacity by the weight of one car: 35,924,000 ÷ 3,353 ≈ 10,700 cars. The answer is an estimate because the conversion factor 2.2 is rounded and because 1,524 kilograms is an average car mass rather than an exact one. 'About 10,700 cars' reports the result honestly; a figure like 10,714.6 would claim precision the inputs never had.

questions.stem: 1 kilometer ≈ 0.6 mile. About how many miles is 5 kilometers?
questions.explanation: Scale the conversion factor by 5: 0.6 × 5 = 3 miles.
choiceFeedback: That adds 5 + 0.6 instead of scaling the ratio.
A kilometer is shorter than a mile, so the number of miles must be smaller than 5.
hints: Write the conversion factor as a ratio: 1 : 0.6.
Multiply both parts by 5.
questions.stemEs: 1 kilómetro ≈ 0.6 millas. ¿Aproximadamente cuántas millas son 5 kilómetros?
questions.explanationEs: Escala el factor de conversión por 5: 0.6 × 5 = 3 millas.
hintsEs: Escribe el factor de conversión como una razón: 1 : 0.6.
Multiplica las dos partes por 5.

questions.stem: 1 pound ≈ 0.45 kilogram. About how many kilograms is 10 pounds?
choiceFeedback: That converts the wrong direction — a kilogram is heavier than a pound.
hints: The ratio is 1 lb : 0.45 kg.
Multiply both parts by 10.
questions.stemEs: 1 libra ≈ 0.45 kilogramos. ¿Aproximadamente cuántos kilogramos son 10 libras?
hintsEs: La razón es 1 lb : 0.45 kg.
Multiplica las dos partes por 10.

questions.stem: Which pair of units comes from two DIFFERENT measurement systems?
questions.explanation: Miles are customary and kilometers are metric, so comparing them requires a between-systems conversion. The other pairs stay inside one system.
choiceFeedback: Both inches and feet are customary.
Both cups and quarts are customary.
Both grams and kilograms are metric.
hints: Sort each unit as customary or metric.
Metric units include meter, gram, liter and their prefixes.
Which pair has one of each?
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál par de unidades viene de dos sistemas de medidas DISTINTOS?
questions.explanationEs: Las millas son del sistema usual y los kilómetros del métrico, así que compararlos requiere una conversión entre sistemas. Los otros pares se quedan dentro de un solo sistema.
hintsEs: Clasifica cada unidad como usual o métrica.
Las unidades métricas incluyen metro, gramo, litro y sus prefijos.
¿Cuál par tiene uno de cada uno?

steps: 1. Identify the conversion ratio connecting systems (e.g. 1 in = 2.54 cm, 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lbs)
2. Set up a ratio table or proportion aligning customary and metric units
3. Multiply or divide by the conversion factor to compute the equivalent measurement
reviewHighlights.watchOut: Compare measurements only after converting to a common unit. Also check whether the conversion factor is exact or rounded: 1 inch = 2.54 cm and 1 international mile = 1.609344 km are exact; 1 mile ≈ 1.609 km is rounded. Use ≈ when the factor or the result has been rounded.

level1.stem: Use 1 kilometer ≈ 0.6 mile. About how many miles is 60 kilometers?
level1.stemEs: Usa 1 kilómetro ≈ 0.6 milla. ¿Más o menos cuántas millas son 60 kilómetros?
hints: Find the scale factor from 1 to 60. Multiply 0.6 by the same factor.
hintsEs: Halla el factor de escala de 1 a 60. Multiplica 0.6 por el mismo factor.
level1.explanation: Write the conversion fact in the table: 1 km : 0.6 mi Find the scale factor from 1 to 60: 60 ÷ 1 = 60 Multiply the miles by the same factor: 0.6 × 60 = 36
level1.explanationEs: Escribe el dato de conversión en la tabla: 1 km : 0.6 mi Halla el factor de escala de 1 a 60: 60 ÷ 1 = 60 Multiplica las millas por el mismo factor: 0.6 × 60 = 36

level2.stem: A sign says the next town is 50 kilometers away. Sam says that is 50 miles. Use 1 kilometer ≈ 0.6 mile. About how many miles away is the town?
level2.stemEs: Un letrero dice que el próximo pueblo está a 50 kilómetros. Sam dice que son 50 millas. Usa 1 kilómetro ≈ 0.6 milla. ¿Más o menos a cuántas millas está el pueblo?

hintsEs: Los kilómetros y las millas son unidades distintas. Convierte antes de decir qué tan lejos está.
level2.explanation: Write the conversion fact in the table: 1 km : 0.6 mi Find the scale factor from 1 to 50: 50 ÷ 1 = 50 Multiply the miles by the same factor: 0.6 × 50 = 30
level2.explanationEs: Escribe el dato de conversión en la tabla: 1 km : 0.6 mi Halla el factor de escala de 1 a 50: 50 ÷ 1 = 50 Multiplica las millas por el mismo factor: 0.6 × 50 = 30

hintsEs: Halla el factor de escala de 1 a 8. Multiplica 0.6 por el mismo factor.

level2.explanationEs: Escribe el dato de conversión en la tabla: 1 km : 0.6 mi Halla el factor de escala de 1 a 8: 8 ÷ 1 = 8 Multiplica las millas por el mismo factor: 0.6 × 8 = 4.8 Compara las dos carreras en millas: 4.8 < 5

level3.stem: A backpack weighs 5 kilograms. Using 1 kilogram ≈ 2.2 pounds, about how much does it weigh in pounds?
choiceFeedback: That divides 5 by 2.2. The conversion multiplies, since each kilogram IS 2.2 pounds.
That adds 5 and 2.2. Use the conversion factor as a multiplier: 5 x 2.2.
That uses 2 pounds per kilogram instead of 2.2. The extra 0.2 per kilogram adds a full pound over five.

level3.stem: Kim changes 6 inches to centimeters. Use 1 inch = 2.54 centimeters. She divides and gets about 2.4 centimeters. What is the correct number of centimeters?
level3.stemEs: Kim cambia 6 pulgadas a centímetros. Usa 1 pulgada = 2.54 centímetros. Ella divide y obtiene más o menos 2.4 centímetros. ¿Cuál es el número correcto de centímetros?
hints: Which unit is shorter, an inch or a centimeter? Should the number get bigger or smaller?
hintsEs: ¿Qué unidad es más corta, una pulgada o un centímetro? ¿El número debe crecer o hacerse más pequeño?
level3.explanation: Compare the unit sizes: 1 cm < 1 in. Write the conversion fact in the table: 1 in. : 2.54 cm Find the scale factor from 1 to 6: 6 ÷ 1 = 6 Multiply the centimeters by the same factor: 2.54 × 6 = 15.24
level3.explanationEs: Compara el tamaño de las unidades: 1 cm < 1 in. Escribe el dato de conversión en la tabla: 1 in. : 2.54 cm Halla el factor de escala de 1 a 6: 6 ÷ 1 = 6 Multiplica los centímetros por el mismo factor: 2.54 × 6 = 15.24

level3.stem: Use 1 kilometer ≈ 0.6 mile. About how many kilometers is 4.2 miles?

level3.explanation: Write the conversion fact in the table: 1 km : 0.6 mi Find the scale factor from 0.6 to 4.2: 4.2 ÷ 0.6 = 7 Multiply the kilometers by the same factor: 1 × 7 = 7
level3.explanationEs: Escribe el dato de conversión en la tabla: 1 km : 0.6 mi Halla el factor de escala de 0.6 a 4.2: 4.2 ÷ 0.6 = 7 Multiplica los kilómetros por el mismo factor: 1 × 7 = 7

level3.stem: A water jug holds 19 liters. Use 1 gallon ≈ 3.8 liters. About how many gallons does the jug hold?

level3.explanation: Write the conversion fact in the table: 1 gal : 3.8 L Find the scale factor from 3.8 to 19: 19 ÷ 3.8 = 5 Multiply the gallons by the same factor: 1 × 5 = 5
level3.explanationEs: Escribe el dato de conversión en la tabla: 1 gal : 3.8 L Halla el factor de escala de 3.8 a 19: 19 ÷ 3.8 = 5 Multiplica los galones por el mismo factor: 1 × 5 = 5

level3.stem: A truck weighs 4,400 pounds. A bridge sign says the limit is 3,000 kilograms. Use 1 kilogram ≈ 2.2 pounds. About how many kilograms under the limit is the truck?
level3.stemEs: Un camión pesa 4,400 libras. Un letrero del puente dice que el límite es 3,000 kilogramos. Usa 1 kilogramo ≈ 2.2 libras. ¿Más o menos cuántos kilogramos por debajo del límite está el camión?
hints: Change the truck's weight to kilograms first. Then compare it with 3,000.
hintsEs: Primero cambia el peso del camión a kilogramos. Luego compáralo con 3,000.
level3.explanation: Write the conversion fact in the table: 1 kg : 2.2 lb Find the scale factor from 2.2 to 4,400: 4,400 ÷ 2.2 = 2,000 Multiply the kilograms by the same factor: 1 × 2,000 = 2,000 Subtract from the limit: 3,000 − 2,000 = 1,000
level3.explanationEs: Escribe el dato de conversión en la tabla: 1 kg : 2.2 lb Halla el factor de escala de 2.2 a 4,400: 4,400 ÷ 2.2 = 2,000 Multiplica los kilogramos por el mismo factor: 1 × 2,000 = 2,000 Resta del límite: 3,000 − 2,000 = 1,000

predict.stem: Before you build the table — 1 kilogram is about 2.2 pounds. About how many pounds is 5 kilograms?
predict.explanation: Scale the unit ratio 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb by 5: 5 × 2.2 ≈ 11 pounds.
choiceFeedback: That treats 5 kilograms and 5 pounds as the same amount. They are different units, so the numbers cannot match.
That divides 5 by 2.2, converting pounds to kilograms instead.

steps.title: Convert one car to pounds
steps.say: Put both amounts in the same unit first.

steps.title: Explain why it is an estimate
steps.say: Rounded inputs give an estimate, not an exact count.

workedSteps.answer: About 10,700 cars. It is an estimate because 2.2 lb per kg is rounded and 1,524 kg is only an average car mass.
